title: Asparagine-related biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
authors: Xia, Jiayi; Cai, Tao; Chen, Peiyin; Gan, Lu; Cao, Bo; Kong, Mingming
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦2型糖尿病的天冬酰胺相关生物标志物，虽含分子对接和转录因子调控网络，但核心是代谢疾病诊断而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a complex metabolic disorder. Emerging evidence suggests asparagine metabolism might play a pivotal role in T2DM, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. This study aimed to detect asparagine-related biomarkers and expound their functional roles in T2DM pathogenesis. METHODS: Transcriptomic datasets from peripheral blood samples of T2DM patients and controls were analyzed. Differential expression analysis, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and machine learning algorithms, followed by expression analysis across cohorts were employed to screen biomarkers. Biomarker diagnostic performance was evaluated. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis, and multi-layer regulatory network construction were conducted. Drug-target interactions and molecular docking were explored to identify potential therapeutics. RESULTS: A total of 90 candidate genes were detected. Four feature genes were screened via multi-algorithm integration. Protein phosphatase 1 catalytic subunit alpha (PPP1CA) and cathepsin D (CTSD) were validated as biomarkers, showing significant upregulation in T2DM samples and high diagnostic accuracy (AUC of PPP1CA = 0.969 and CTSD = 0.984 in the training cohort, AUC of PPP1CA = 0.806 and CTSD = 0.875 in the validation cohort, respectively). Functional enrichment highlighted distinct yet complementary functional roles of PPP1CA and CTSD in T2DM progression. Immune infiltration revealed elevated activated dendritic cells, mast cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells in T2DM samples, with PPP1CA and CTSD correlating significantly with these cell types. Regulatory networks identified shared transcription factors and miRNAs targeting both genes. Pharmacological screening prioritized norcantharidin and naringenin as high-affinity compounds targeting these biomarkers. CONCLUSION: This study identified PPP1CA and CTSD as asparagine-related biomarkers driving immune-metabolic crosstalk in T2DM. The priicted regulatory networks and therapeutic compounds provided novel insights into T2DM mechanisms and potential intervention strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：2型糖尿病（T2DM）是一种复杂的代谢性疾病。新近证据提示天冬酰胺代谢可能在T2DM中发挥关键作用，但其潜在分子机制仍不明确。本研究旨在检测天冬酰胺相关生物标志物，并阐明其在T2DM发病机制中的功能角色。方法：分析T2DM患者及对照组外周血样本的转录组数据集。采用差异表达分析、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络及机器学习算法，随后进行跨队列表达分析以筛选生物标志物。评估生物标志物的诊断性能。进行功能富集、免疫浸润分析及多层调控网络构建。探索药物-靶点相互作用及分子对接以识别潜在治疗药物。结果：共检测到90个候选基因。通过多算法整合筛选出四个特征基因。蛋白磷酸酶1催化亚基α（PPP1CA）和组织蛋白酶D（CTSD）被验证为生物标志物，在T2DM样本中显著上调，且具有高诊断准确性（训练队列中PPP1CA的AUC = 0.969，CTSD的AUC = 0.984；验证队列中PPP1CA的AUC = 0.806，CTSD的AUC = 0.875）。功能富集凸显了PPP1CA和CTSD在T2DM进展中独特且互补的功能角色。免疫浸润分析显示，T2DM样本中活化的树突状细胞、肥大细胞及髓源性抑制细胞升高，且PPP1CA和CTSD与这些细胞类型显著相关。调控网络识别出靶向这两个基因的共享转录因子和miRNA。药理学筛选优先将去甲斑蝥素和柚皮素列为靶向这些生物标志物的高亲和力化合物。结论：本研究将PPP1CA和CTSD鉴定为驱动T2DM中免疫-代谢串扰的天冬酰胺相关生物标志物。预测的调控网络及治疗化合物为T2DM机制和潜在干预策略提供了新见解。
